notes: Overall a very clean, well-structured implementation. Scores and issues by category: ARCHITECTURAL ADHERENCE (7/10): The most significant violation is that the Router performs cross-service lookups directly (e.g., calling userService.getUserById() before calling projectService.addMember(), calling taskService.getTaskById() before calling commentService.createComment(), calling userService.getUserById() before calling taskService.assignTask()). While the requirement says 'no direct service-to-service calls' and the router is technically the HTTP layer, passing taskTitle and assigneeId as parameters to commentService.createComment() is an awkward coupling that leaks task internals through the router into the comment service — this is a design smell even if not a strict rule violation. The event bus is otherwise used correctly for all notifications. COMPLETENESS (9/10): All services are implemented with full CRUD. All three events (task.assigned, task.status_changed, comment.added) are published and handled. The demo script is thorough and exercises all features including edge cases. Minor gap: no PATCH support (acceptable since PUT is used), no pagination, and there is no GET /notifications/:id route tested in the demo. The description says 'get comments on tasks' but there's no update comment operation (acceptable per spec). CODE QUALITY (9/10): Excellent TypeScript typing with EventPayloadMap providing full type safety on the event bus. Clean separation of concerns, consistent error handling patterns, good use of private methods in the router, proper UUID generation, ISO timestamps, input trimming/validation. The readBody helper is clean. Minor issues: use of 'any' in demo.ts is reasonable for a demo; the Router class is large (could be split further) but acceptable per constraints. CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE (8/10): Violation 1 — Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls): The router calls multiple services in sequence to fulfill one request (e.g., userService then projectService for member add, taskService then commentService for comment create), which is not strictly inter-service communication but does blur the line. Violation 2 — Rule 2 (each service owns its data exclusively): commentService.createComment() accepts taskTitle and assigneeId as parameters supplied by the router after reading from taskService — this means task data is being passed through the router into the comment service rather than being obtained via event, which is a minor but real data ownership concern. All other constraints (no npm deps, each service in own file, forward-only transitions, in-memory stores, built-in http module) are cleanly respected.
